land.text: South Prussia of 1793: the Poznań, Kalisz and Gniezno voivodeships of Greater Poland (south of the Netze District), the lands of Sieradz and Łęczyca, the Kuyavian voivodeship of Brześć and Dobrzyń Land, and adjacent parts of the Płock and Rawa voivodeships; without Thorn (West Prussia) and the Lesser Poland land south of the Pilica

correction.text: South Prussia of 1793: the Poznań, Kalisz and Gniezno voivodeships of Greater Poland (south of the Netze District), the lands of Sieradz and Łęczyca, the Kuyavian voivodeship of Brześć and Dobrzyń Land, and adjacent parts of the Płock and Rawa voivodeships; without Thorn (West Prussia) and the Lesser Poland land south of the Pilica

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row; its Kingdom of Prussia and Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth shapes draw the land). Redrawn after review: the first shape used the gazetteer region 'Kuyavia', which is the whole Kuyavian-Pomeranian voivodeship (19,726 km2) with Toruń, Chełmno, Grudziądz and Bydgoszcz, West Prussia's land (27,060 km2 of overlap with west-prussia, 38% of this shape), against the South Prussia page, which takes from Kuyavia only 'the Kuyavian voivodeship of Brześć' (with Dobrzyń Land). The shape is now Greater Poland + Łódź + the Kuyavian-Pomeranian voivodeship minus the Chełmno Land polygon (royal-prussia/west-prussia's line: the Brześć Kujawski voivodeship and Dobrzyń Land remain), minus the Netze District (the page: South Prussia 'bordered ... on the Prussian Netze District in the north'; the Netze District, 1772, held Wałcz, Kamień, Bydgoszcz, Inowrocław), minus the Lesser Poland land south and east of the Pilica ('In the southeast the Pilica river marked the border with those Lesser Polish territories') and minus the Toruń disc (Thorn is West Prussia's): 53,130 km2 on the grid. The Second Partition: Prussia took 58,000 km2 of 'Gniezno, Poznań, Sieradz, Kalisz, Płock, Brześć Kujawski and Inowrocław voivodeships, Dobrzyń Land and parts of the Kraków, Rawa and Masovian voivodeships', organised as South Prussia, 'and the cities of Danzig and Thorn', which went to West Prussia: 53,130 + Danzig and Thorn discs (3,289) = 56,419 km2, ratio 0.97. Inowrocław itself is in the Netze District (west-prussia) in this dossier. Parts of the Kraków voivodeship (Radomsko is inside via Łódź; Częstochowa is not) are not drawn.

correction.text: South Prussia of 1795 with Warsaw, without Dobrzyń Land northeast of the Vistula (New East Prussia)

keyframe_review.note: 1795: Warsaw 'was added in 1795 after the Third Partition' and 'the lands of Dobrzyń and Płock northeast of the Vistula river were transferred to New East Prussia' (the Dobrzyń Land part is cut by a polygon along the Vistula; Włocławek stays). 53,000 km2 in 1806 with 1,503,508 people on the infobox; drawn 59,455 km2 on the grid, ratio 1.12 (within the factor of two; the 50 km Warsaw disc, 8,855 km2, and the Łódź voivodeship stand-in are generous). Redrawn after review; overlap with west-prussia 0. Borders (South Prussia page): the Brandenburgian Neumark in the west, the Prussian Netze District in the north, the Pilica river in the southeast against the Lesser Poland territories that 'in 1795 became part of Austrian New Galicia', and in the southwest Prussian Silesia and New Silesia, 'a smaller province including the former Duchy of Siewierz, which was administered from South Prussia' (created October 1795, New Silesia page: 'later largely administered by South Prussia', capital Siewierz, area not given). New Silesia is not drawn here.

region.text: South Prussia of 1793: the Poznań, Kalisz and Gniezno voivodeships of Greater Poland (south of the Netze District), the lands of Sieradz and Łęczyca, the Kuyavian voivodeship of Brześć and Dobrzyń Land, and adjacent parts of the Płock and Rawa voivodeships; without Thorn (West Prussia) and the Lesser Poland land south of the Pilica

ledger.note: 25 September 1793: the Second Partition gives Prussia South Prussia. 'On 23 January 1793, Prussia signed a treaty with Russia'; 'This was accepted by the Grodno Sejm on 23 September' (or 25 September, sources vary); the South Prussia infobox dates the province from 25 September 1793. Prussia's share was 58,000 km2. Shape redrawn after review (see the keyframe note): 53,130 km2 + Danzig and Thorn = 56,419 km2 against the page's 58,000.

1795: Warsaw is added. 'The capital of the province was Poznań (1793-1795) at first, afterwards Warsaw (1795-1806), which was added in 1795 after the Third Partition'; Prussia took 'Podlachia, the remainder of Masovia, and Warsaw' (Third Partition page).

region.text: the lands of Dobrzyń and Płock northeast of the Vistula (the part that belonged to South Prussia: Dobrzyń Land)

ledger.note: 1795: 'After the Third Partition, the lands of Dobrzyń and Płock northeast of the Vistula river were transferred to New East Prussia'. The loss region is Dobrzyń Land only: the Płock voivodeship land was not drawn in South Prussia.

region.text: South Prussia of 1795 with Warsaw, without Dobrzyń Land northeast of the Vistula (New East Prussia)

ledger.note: 1806: the Greater Poland Uprising ('took place in 1806', no date on the page) after Napoleon's victory in the War of the Fourth Coalition; South Prussia is contested until the Treaties of Tilsit. Counterpart changed from duchy-of-warsaw after review: the Duchy of Warsaw did not exist before the Treaties of Tilsit (9 July 1807); kingdom-of-prussia /ledger/35-36 books the contest with first-french-empire, 1806-10 to 1807-07.

wars.outcome: After the Polish-Russian War of 1792 Prussia took 58,000 km2 and Russia 250,000 km2; the Commonwealth 'lost about 307,000 km2, being reduced to 215,000 km2'.
wars.note: A partition by treaty (23 January 1793), ratified at Grodno on 22 July (Russian share) and 23 or 25 September 1793 (Prussian share).

zones.text: South Prussia of 1795 with Warsaw, without Dobrzyń Land northeast of the Vistula (New East Prussia)

wars.outcome: Napoleon's victory and the uprising of 1806 ended Prussian rule; the Treaties of Tilsit (9 July 1807) gave South Prussia to the Duchy of Warsaw.
wars.note: The page gives the year of the uprising, not the dates. The Duchy of Warsaw was created at Tilsit (9 July 1807), so the 1806 contest is with the French Empire (counterpart changed after review).

certainty.note: Partition treaty lines (1793, 1795) and river borders (the Pilica, the Netze District line); the pages list voivodeships, not survey lines, so the sharp level rests on the treaties and the drawn polygons are approximate.

notes:
The Prussian partition zone of 1793, a state Cliopatria lacks. Typed colony (Prussian province, a tint of kingdom-of-prussia). The shape is a union of gazetteer admin-1 areas (Greater Poland, Łódź) and the south of the Kuyavian-Pomeranian voivodeship, cut by polygons; Thorn and Danzig (1793) are in west-prussia, not here.

Repaired after the review (2026-10-31): (1) {region: Kuyavia} replaced by the Kuyavian-Pomeranian voivodeship minus a Chełmno Land polygon (the Brześć Kujawski voivodeship and Dobrzyń Land stay), and the Netze District, the Lesser Poland land south of the Pilica and a Toruń disc subtracted: overlap with west-prussia 0, area 53,130 km2 (1793) and 59,455 km2 (1795, ratio 1.12 to the infobox's 53,000 for 1806). The Kuyavia line agreed with west-prussia and royal-prussia: Brześć Kujawski and Dobrzyń to South Prussia; Chełmno Land and Toruń to Royal Prussia / West Prussia; Inowrocław and Bydgoszcz to the Netze District (west-prussia, 1775-1807, per the Netze District page, which lists Inowrocław among its divisions), although the Second Partition page lists the Inowrocław voivodeship among South Prussia's 1793 land (the voivodeship was split: its western part went in 1772). (2) The 1806 contest names first-french-empire instead of duchy-of-warsaw (created at Tilsit). (3) The 1795-96 borders: the South Prussia page gives them in words (Pilica, Neumark, Netze District, Prussian Silesia and New Silesia, Austrian New Galicia); New Silesia has no dossier.

Not settled: (1) The date of the Dobrzyń and Płock transfer is the Third Partition (24 October 1795, month from the New East Prussia infobox); the new-east-prussia dossier draws 45 km and 30 km circles that cross the Vistula (Włocławek) and should be clipped by this polygon (the reviewer's fix for new-east-prussia). (2) 'Parts of the Kraków, Rawa and Masovian voivodeships' (Second Partition page) are drawn only as far as the Łódź voivodeship reaches. (3) The South Prussia page gives 25 September 1793, the Second Partition page 23 or 25 September: month 9 kept. (4) The Pilica line is a polygon: Opoczno and Tomaszów are cut, Piotrków and Rawa kept. (5) Three departments (Posen, Kalisch, Warschau) are on the page but their extent is not. (6) The Warsaw disc (50 km) is generous. (7) The gazetteer region 'Kuyavia' (19,726 km2, the whole Kuyavian-Pomeranian voivodeship) is the root of the double drawing; Brześć Kujawski Voivodeship and Chełmno Land should be regions.
